Peri-implant bone characteristics of dental implants retrieved from humans: a systematic review and meta-analysis
records.description: This dataset contains data extracted for a systematic review and meta-analysis of peri-implant bone histological outcomes in humans. It includes four Excel files covering bone-to-implant contact (BIC; 63 studies, 176 estimates), bone density within the threads (BDWT; 22 studies, 61 estimates), bone density outside the threads (BDOT; 18 studies, 47 estimates), and the distance between the implant platform and the first bone-to-implant contact (fBIC; 4 studies, 12 estimates). Each row represents outcome data for a study arm or intervention, including the number of implants evaluated, the mean, and the standard deviation. Study characteristics and candidate moderators are provided where applicable. The accompanying README describes the files, variables, units, and coding conventions. The review was registered in PROSPERO under CRD42023430289, and the literature search was last updated in June 2026.

CLINICAL AND RADIOGRAPHIC EVALUATION OF LONG-TERM OUTCOMES OF ENDODONTIC TREATMENT OF CHRONIC APICAL PERIODONTITIS
records.description: Abstract. A clinical and radiographic evaluation of long-term outcomes of endodontic treatment of chronic apical periodontitis was performed in 56 patients. Treatment effectiveness was assessed based on changes in clinical symptoms, the degree of periapical bone healing, and the preservation of tooth function at 6 and 12 months. The rate of complete radiographic healing increased from 30.4% to 42.9%, while the overall proportion of patients demonstrating complete or partial periapical tissue healing reached 85.7% at 12 months. Absence of spontaneous pain was recorded in 94.6% of patients, and tooth function was preserved in 96.4%. Differences were identified between the resolution of clinical symptoms and the radiographic restoration of periapical structures.

records.description: Odontogenic infections remain one of the most pressing problems in modern maxillofacial surgery and dentistry. Despite significant advances in diagnosis and treatment, these pathological conditions can progress rapidly and lead to severe outcomes, requiring ongoing analysis of modern approaches to their management. The last decade has seen a significant increase in the incidence of purulent-inflammatory diseases of the maxillofacial region, with phlegmons posing the greatest threat to the health and lives of patients.

records.title: COMPREHENSIVE PATHOGENETIC THERAPY OF COMBINED PERIODONTAL AND DENTAL HARD TISSUE PATHOLOGY IN PATIENTS WITH ENDEMIC IODINE DEFICIENCY
records.description: Endemic iodine deficiency remains a widespread public health concern that triggers systemic metabolic alterations, predominantly characterized by thyroid axis dysfunction and impaired calcium-phosphate homeostasis. Reduced functional activity of the thyroid gland detrimentally affects the maxillofacial system: it suppresses reparative osteogenesis and connective tissue remodeling within the periodontium, reduces the remineralizing capacity of oral fluid, and decreases salivary levels of secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA). Consequently, this systemic milieu accelerates enamel demineralization and promotes the progression of generalized inflammatory periodontal diseases.

records.title: MODERN APPROACHES TO THE TREATMENT OF DENTOFACIAL ANOMALIES USING BRACKET SYSTEMS
records.description: This article highlights modern approaches to the treatment of dentofacial anomalies using bracket systems. Orthodontic anomalies adversely affect not only the aesthetic alignment of the dentition but also masticatory function, phonetics, periodontal structures, and oral hygiene. The study examines the clinical characteristics, indications, diagnostic workflows, and therapeutic phases of metallic, ceramic, lingual, and self-ligating bracket systems, alongside their biomechanical principles, oral hygiene protocols, potential complications, and retention management. Furthermore, the role of contemporary digital orthodontic workflows—including intraoral scanning and three-dimensional (3D) treatment planning—is comprehensively evaluated.

records.description: Protraction facemasks and maxillary expansion appliances are widely used orthopedic modalities for modifying maxillofacial relationships in growing patients with maxillary deficiency. Their clinical effects vary substantially according to anchorage design, force application, expansion protocol, and the relative contribution of skeletal and dentoalveolar adaptation. Conventional tooth-borne rapid maxillary expansion combined with facemask therapy can produce clinically relevant maxillary advancement but may also be associated with dental compensation and vertical skeletal changes. In contrast, hybrid and skeletal anchorage-supported systems, including hybrid-Hyrax, miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion, and bone-anchored maxillary protraction, have been developed to improve orthopedic force transmission and reduce undesirable dental effects. records.title: IMPROVING ORTHODONTIC CARE FOR SCHOOL AGED CHILDREN AND EARLY MANAGEMENT OF SKELETAL CRANIOFACIAL DISCREPANCIES
records.description: This narrative review examines timely orthodontic care for school aged children with skeletal craniofacial discrepancies. It distinguishes early detection from immediate appliance treatment and considers dental and skeletal outcomes separately. A proposed care pathway combines initial screening, specialist assessment, individualized timing and longitudinal follow-up. Early intervention should address a defined clinical problem, while routine two-phase treatment cannot be assumed to improve final outcomes in every child. The proposed service indicators require prospective validation; no original patient data are reported.

records.description: Bone deficiency is one of the most important anatomical factors affecting the planning and success of dental implant treatment. Accurate evaluation of the quantity, quality, and morphology of the alveolar bone is essential for determining the optimal implant position and the need for additional bone augmentation procedures. Modern diagnostic methods, particularly cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), provide detailed three-dimensional information about bone height, width, cortical thickness, and the relationship between the implant site and adjacent anatomical structures. The integration of CBCT with intraoral scanning, virtual implant planning, three-dimensional reconstruction, and computer-guided technologies significantly improves diagnostic accuracy and treatment predictability. In addition, emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and three-dimensional printing offer new possibilities for individualized treatment planning. records.title: TEMPOROMANDIBULAR DISORDERS: DEVELOPMENTAL MECHANISMS, CLINICAL COURSE, DIAGNOSIS AND CONTEMPORARY MANAGEMENT — A NARRATIVE REVIEW OF CURRENT EVIDENCE
records.description: Background. Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of painful and functional conditions of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ), the masticatory muscles and functionally associated orofacial structures, classified under ICD-10 code M26.6. Over the past two decades the conceptual model of TMD has shifted from an occlusion-centred mechanical paradigm to a multifactorial biopsychosocial framework. Aim. To synthesise current evidence on the aetiology and molecular pathogenesis of TMDs, to characterise the clinical course of their principal phenotypes, to appraise the performance of contemporary diagnostic instruments, and to systematise evidence-based treatment principles. Methods. A narrative review with a structured literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and the Cochrane Library for records published between January 2005 and May 2026. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, network meta-analyses and clinical practice guidelines.

records.title: EVALUATING THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN MANDIBULAR PLANE AND LOWER OCCLUSAL PLANE IN FULLY DENTULOUS PATIENTS
records.description: Purpose: The inclination of the occlusal plane is important for diagnostic purposes, and it also acts as a guideline for designing occlusal rehabilitation therapies. When all teeth are lost, different landmarks have been employed to establish the occlusal plane. Hence, this study aims to compare the mandibular plane with the lower occlusal plane in dentulous patients. Methods: A digital photograph of the right and left facial profiles was obtained of the angle between the intraoral occlusal plane (represented by a modified Fox plane) and mandibular plane (represented by a metallic scale placed on the lower border of the mandible) in a standard position. The angle was calculated using Microdicom software, and results were statistically analysed using Mann Whitney U test . Results: The average angle between the occlusal plane and mandibular plane was 6 degrees and the difference in angle between the right and left sides was not statistically significant.
